hint.text: There has to be a capital letter for the first word in the line of speech.

instruction.text: Choose either the capitalised or lowercase version of the word to make the speech correct.

atoms.b: “((++I i)) am really excited for your birthday!” said Emma.
“((++We we)) are going to Spain next week,” Uncle Sam told us.
“Athens is such a beautiful city. ((++You you)) have to visit!” Charlie told us.

end.text: There always needs to be a capital letter at the start of a sentence.
The first word after the speech mark does not need to be capitalised, unless there’s a full stop before the last speech mark.

atoms.b: ((++You you)) said that you liked painting.

end.text: Even in reported speech where there are no speech marks, there has to be a capital letter at the start like any sentence.

atoms.b: Patrick ((++said Said)) that his mum comes from Ireland too.
“((++How how)) many siblings do you have?” ((++asked Asked)) Chris.
